I ran the `/code-conventions --review-pr` checklist over `f6f337674b…HEAD`. That range is one commit, `e22f39d49 fix(tests): resolve post-Vitest flaky tests`, touching 63 files (+78/−70). I found no rule failures, only three low-severity nits.

**Mode:** `--review-pr`. I considered all 60 rules in `rules.json` and checked every item off. `docs/engineering/pr-self-review-checklist.generated.md` isn't gitignored in this repo, so I wrote the checklist to the scratchpad instead of the repo.

**What the diff does**
- 67 `await app.close()` calls became `await app?.close()` across the integration specs, so a failed `beforeAll`/`beforeEach` no longer hides the real error behind a `TypeError`. The repo already used this pattern before the PR: `src/app.provider.spec.ts`, `oidc-auth.controller.integration.spec.ts` and `auth.controller.integration.spec.ts`. After this change no plain `await app.close()` is left in any `*.spec.ts`; the `e2e-spec` files are intentionally not touched.
- `nameBuilder` now runs `sanitizeName` again after truncating, so a name cut at a space doesn't end with trailing whitespace.
- The bridge-name negative test now draws a new random noun until it gets one that isn't a real bridge name, using the existing `isBridgeName` helper.

**Rules that applied and passed:** CHANGE-01, CHANGE-02, NAME-01, REUSE-01 (reuses `isBridgeName` and `sanitizeName` rather than adding helpers), STYLE-01 (both non-obvious changes have a short comment explaining why), TEST-01, TEST-05, TEST-06 and TEST-08. All 63 changed files have the SPDX header. The rest (auth, DB, cache, config, routes, logging, security, resilience, etc.) don't apply to this diff.

**Zoom:** Level 1 for TEST-09 only. I didn't need Level 2.

## Findings

1. **Unnecessary `?.` inside an existing `if (app)` check (CHANGE-01 / NAME-01, low)**
   - `src/modules/chains/feature-flags/feature-flag.service.integration.spec.ts:23`: `if (app) await app?.close();`
   - `src/modules/messages/routes/messages.controller.integration.spec.ts:49-50`: `if (app) { await app?.close(); }`

   The `if (app)` check already rules out `undefined`, so the `?.` only adds noise. This looks like a side effect of the bulk find-and-replace. Fix: go back to `app.close()` inside the check, or drop the check and keep only `await app?.close()`.

2. **Unnecessary `?.` on a local `const` that is always set (CHANGE-01, low)**
   - `src/modules/chains/feature-flags/feature-flag.service.integration.spec.ts:97`: `await app?.close();`

   Here `app` is a local `const app = await new TestAppProvider().provide(...)` declared a few lines up (line 88), and `app.init()` has already been called on it. It can't be `undefined` at this point, so the change there is pure churn. Fix: go back to `await app.close();`.

3. **No test that always hits the truncation edge case (TEST-09, low)**
   - `src/domain/common/entities/name.builder.ts:26-28`

   The fix covers truncation at `NAME_MAX_LENGTH` (30) landing just after a space. The only coverage is the existing 50 random runs in `name.builder.spec.ts:13-19`, and those hit this case only when `faker.person.fullName()` is longer than 30 characters with a space at position 30. That is rare, so the regression isn't tested reliably. TEST-09 asks for edge-case tests when the edge case is part of the behaviour. Fix: add a test that mocks `faker.person.fullName` (or picks the sample) to return a long name with a space at index 29, then asserts `NameSchema.parse` succeeds and `sanitizeName(name) === name`.

No code or doc changes were made (review only). No rule failures remain; items 1–3 are optional clean-ups for the author.
